problem: REVERIE (high-level instruction, remote object grounding) is defined on discrete navigation graphs, which is unrealistic for real robots that must execute long sequences of low-level actions in continuous space.
motivation: Real-world navigation requires continuous low-level control, and high-level instructions are more natural for humans. Combining REVERIE-style instructions with a continuous environment makes the task closer to the physical world.
key_idea: Introduce the REVE-CE task (REVERIE in continuous environments with low-level actions) and a multi-branch cross-modal attention (MBCMA) framework as a baseline for it.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation or analysis details can be reported. The abstract claims that MBCMA greatly outperforms state-of-the-art VLN baselines adapted to REVE-CE.
method: REVE-CE task: extends REVERIE to a continuous environment where the agent executes a much longer sequence of low-level actions given high-level instructions.
MBCMA framework: multi-branch cross-modal attention model for fusing language and visual inputs to solve REVE-CE (details not available from the abstract).

setting.backbone: MBCMA multi-branch cross-modal attention network (trained; details not given in abstract)
setting.training_data: not stated in abstract (presumably REVERIE-derived instructions in continuous environments)

results: The abstract states that MBCMA greatly outperforms state-of-the-art VLN baselines and establishes a new benchmark for REVE-CE. No numbers are given.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so details are unknown.
Evaluated in simulation only, as far as the abstract indicates.
